questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Navigating the Filesystem”?
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Current working directory” under lesson 12, “Navigating the Filesystem”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Navigating the Filesystem”?
options: Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
Use commands and arguments deliberately, and inspect stdout, stderr, and the exit status separately.
questions.answer_key: Use commands and arguments deliberately, and inspect stdout, stderr, and the exit status separately.
questions.explanation: Use commands and arguments deliberately, and inspect stdout, stderr, and the exit status separately. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Navigating the Filesystem”?
options: Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
Validate the exact target, use a preview for side effects, and verify the result before reporting success.
Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
questions.answer_key: Validate the exact target, use a preview for side effects, and verify the result before reporting success.
questions.explanation: Validate the exact target, use a preview for side effects, and verify the result before reporting success. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
